full_judgment: Mustafa Kamal, J :- Both the defendant-petitioners and the plaintiff-respondents claimed exchange of the suit property belonging to the admitted owner Dhirendra Nath Acharya and others with their respective properties in India. The plaintiff’s case is that a General power of Attorney was executed by the said Acharya and others on 20-2-65 and the plaintiff's deed of exchange is dated 23-2-65. The plaintiff claims possession of the suit land and recording of his name in the R. S. Khatian as a possessor by way of exchange. In Exchange Case no.36 of 1970-71.the plaintiff applied for permission for registration of the exchange deed before the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi. But defendant no. 2, Predecessor of the present petitioners, filed an objection in the said exchange case alleging that defendant no. 1 exchanged the suit land with his properties in India from the same Acharya and others by a deed of exchange registered on 9-2-68 by one Saifuddin Mondal on the strength of a General power of Attorney executed by the said Acharya and others. The suit land was purchased by defendant no. 2 on 9-2-68, i.e. on the same date from defendant No. 1 After inquiry the Deputy Commissioner found that the deed of exchange of the plaintiff was genuine and that of defendant no. I was forged. He recommended to the Government for registration of the exchange deed of the plaintiff. The Government Instructed the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi to advise the plaintiff to seek relief in a competent court on the ground that one exchange deed had already been registered in favour of defendant no. I on 9.2.68 with respect to the same suit land. It is the further case of the plaintiff that defendant no.1 got the deed of exchange and the power of Attorney by false personation. His suit was for a declaration for his right to possess the suit land and also for a declaration that the power of attorney of defendant No.1 is forged and that the defendants did not acquire any right title and interest in the suit land, Defendant No.2 in his written statement reiterated his case as made out in his objection in Exchange Case No.36 of 1970-71.
